players.product: specialty / legacy DRAM (DDR4 / LPDDR4), CUBE custom memory and NOR flash

quarterly_data.signal: 2Q26 consolidated results (deck, unaudited): net sales NT$59,843 million, +56.4% QoQ and +184.7% YoY (2Q25 NT$21,018 million); gross margin 66.2% (1Q26 53.4%, 2Q25 22.7%); operating profit NT$28,979 million, operating margin 48.4% (2Q25 operating loss); net income NT$24,199 million; EPS NT$5.40 (1Q26 NT$2.25); 1H26 EPS NT$7.65; EBITDA NT$33,643 million.
quarterly_data.figure: 2Q26 net sales NT$59,843 million (+184.7% YoY); gross margin 66.2%; EPS NT$5.40

quarterly_data.signal: Memory business 2Q26 (deck): net sales NT$51,700 million (+72.8% QoQ, +303.1% YoY), gross margin 70.3% (2Q25 12.1%), operating margin 56.9%. CMS (Customized Memory Solution, formerly the DRAM business): revenue +78% QoQ and +467% YoY, 'supported by strong AI demand'; bit shipments decreased low-teens% QoQ and increased low-twenties% YoY; blended ASP (US$) increased by ~100% QoQ, 'reflecting a rise in pure ASP and a favorable product mix', and over 300% YoY; 20nm revenue continued to step up, with further growth expected over the coming quarters.
quarterly_data.figure: memory net sales NT$51,700 million (+303.1% YoY); memory gross margin 70.3%; CMS revenue +467% YoY; CMS blended ASP ~100% QoQ

quarterly_data.signal: Flash business 2Q26 (deck): revenue +65% QoQ and +176% YoY; bit shipments increased mid-teens% QoQ and YoY; blended ASP (US$) increased low-forties% QoQ and more than doubled YoY; revenue contribution from 24nm and 32nm SLC NAND increased significantly, with momentum expected to continue. Memory revenue by application QoQ in 2Q26: computer +89%, communication +82%, consumer +64%, car & industrial +54%. Company claims to be the 'World's No.1 NOR Flash supplier'; by Winbond internal statistics it was #3 in SLC NAND Flash with a 15% share in 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: Flash revenue +65% QoQ, +176% YoY; SLC NAND share 15% (#3, 2025)

quarterly_data.signal: Memory capex (deck, cash basis as of August 6, 2026): 1H26 capex was NT$7.5B; 2026 capex is estimated at approx. NT$39.5B, of which wafer fab equipment (WFE) accounts for ~95%. 2Q26 capex in the cash flow statement NT$5,172 million (1Q26 NT$2,916 million).

Company outlook (deck): demand for high-density NOR continues to outpace supply, supporting a sustained pricing uptrend through 2026 and beyond; SLC NAND supply remains tight, with strong design-ins underpinning the upward pricing trend into 2H26; global DRAM supply remains constrained while major memory suppliers continue to scale back DDR4 bit shipments, with further upside potential in 3Q contract pricing and AI-driven demand reinforcing a positive outlook into 2H26 and 2027. Strong demand cited from AI server, data center, infrastructure, edge AI and automotive. Memory capacity utilization ~100% in 2Q26 (~100% in 1Q26, ~90% in 2Q25); increasing LTA penetration enhances long-term supply resilience and order visibility.

Company (deck, Winbond business outlook): 16nm capacity ramp remains on track, with meaningful contribution expected from 2027; next-phase KH Fab Module B expansion planning is underway; CUBE and Si-Cap are emerging as the next wave of major growth drivers beyond 2027; profitability continues to hit record highs, with confidence in further sequential growth.
